About

Marketing built on diagnosis, evidence and AI systems.

Who I am

I'm Johnson Joel Sonayon, a Digital Marketing & Growth Specialist based in Lagos, Nigeria, with a specialism in AI-assisted marketing systems. I work where digital marketing, growth strategy and responsible technology meet, and I follow one rule: diagnosis before intervention.

Before a campaign runs, I look at the core business problem, the market, the audience, the customer journey and the evidence. My 17-project practical portfolio covers research, SEO, Meta Ads, funnels, analytics and integrated growth strategy, and I built the JJS AI Co-Pilot systems to keep AI inside human-led, reviewed workflows.

I began in design and video, which taught me to tell stories visually, but marketing is where my work is now. Long term, I'm heading towards AI governance and policy. I hold a B.A. in Philosophy from Lagos State University.

Next: The Co-Pilots
JJS AI Co-Pilots

Five co-pilots help me work faster. I stay in charge.

JJS are my initials. The Co-Pilots are structured instructions, checklists and verification steps that run inside Claude, ChatGPT or any large language model.

Why they matter

Speed

Faster research synthesis, competitive analysis and content drafting.

Quality control

Verification checkpoints before any campaign asset or audit report moves forward.

Repeatable work

Ad-hoc marketing tasks become documented, repeatable workflows.

What they are not

They are not autonomous tools and they do not replace my work. Every output is reviewed and approved by me before it is used. They do not guarantee results.

Open the Co-Pilots folder
Custom-built

A Co-Pilot built for your role.

Beyond the five Co-Pilots I built for my own practice, on appointment I build a custom AI-assisted marketing system (a JJS AI Co-Pilot) for the exact role I am hired for and the business I serve. Whatever the role, the Co-Pilot is built for it and is unique to that employer.

A Social Media Manager role gets a Social Media Management Co-Pilot, and an SEO role gets an SEO Co-Pilot. These are illustrations, not limits. It is shaped by the role, the goals the business wants achieved, the problems it faces, and the answers the employer gives during intake, so it supports the delivery of results in that specific job.

A custom Co-Pilot can be built around any of my six focus areas (Diagnosis, Visibility, Credibility, Conversion, Retention and Marketing ROI), and it is not limited to them. The role decides the design. Where a client service falls outside what my five Co-Pilots cover, I build a custom Co-Pilot for that service too. Where the work is already covered, I deliver it with the existing systems.

How a custom Co-Pilot is built

1

Intake

I ask for the goals the business wants the role to achieve, the problems it faces, and the full responsibilities and scope of the role.

2

Design

I build a Co-Pilot around those objectives, with instructions, checklists and verification steps.

3

Operation

The Co-Pilot runs inside Claude, ChatGPT, Google NotebookLM or any large language model to support my research, planning, drafting and reporting.

4

Quality Control

I review and approve every output before it is used.

What the employer gains

Support built for the exact role, diagnosis before spend, deeper research behind decisions, quality-control checkpoints before anything goes out, protection against unsupported claims, consistent documented workflows, and reporting tied to the goals set at intake.

The skills behind the Co-Pilots

The five systems and the custom-built ones are built and operated through three connected skills. I review and approve every output produced through them.

Prompt Engineering

Writing precise, structured instructions that direct AI to produce consistent, on-brief work.

Context Engineering

Giving the AI the right background, rules, data and boundaries so its outputs stay accurate and relevant, applied every time I operate a Co-Pilot.

Vibe Coding (AI-Assisted Development)

Building websites and digital tools by directing AI in plain language and reviewing the results. I built this portfolio website this way, and the same skills let me build websites and digital tools for a business.

Where this is going

Building these systems taught me that powerful AI still needs clear human responsibility. My long-term vision is AI governance and policy: helping organisations decide where AI belongs and where it does not, adopt it responsibly, manage the risks, and keep people accountable for every decision. Marketing is where I'm proving it.
